# Test determinism: advance a clock, don't wait on one

<!-- review-bot-scope:start -->
packages/*/test/**/*.ts
packages/conformance/src/**/*.ts
packages/harness/src/**/*.ts
packages/store-libsql/src/testing.ts
packages/driver/bin/*.ts
<!-- review-bot-scope:end -->

Scope: `packages/*/test/**/*.ts`, `packages/conformance/src/**/*.ts` and `packages/harness/src/**/*.ts` (the fuzz, fault-matrix, invariant and simulator machinery), `packages/store-libsql/src/testing.ts`, and `packages/driver/bin/*.ts` (the hosts the chaos leg spawns). Note `scripts/determinism-lint.sh` already bans ambient time/randomness/timers structurally across `packages/{core,store-libsql,conformance,driver,sdk}/src` — so inside `packages/conformance/src` this rule adds only the shapes that lint cannot see (seed guards, floors, shared state), while `packages/*/test`, `packages/harness/src` and `packages/driver/bin` are territory that lint deliberately excludes ("tests and the harness own their nondeterminism") and this rule governs. Deliberately NOT covered: whether a test asserts the right thing about provenance (the fence-provenance rule) and whether a checker is capable of failing at all (`scripts/lint-selftest.py`, `scripts/mutation-probe.py`).

A test's verdict must be a function of the code under test and its declared seed — never of elapsed wall time, of what else is running on the box, or of the order the suite happened to run in. Two operational forms, both already built here: **invert the time dependency** (engine time is database time, so move it with `admin.setFakeNowEpochMs` or the fixture's `advance()`, never by sleeping and hoping) and **assert on causality, not latency** (a launch count, a row state, a `SimWorld.trace` entry, a `clock.fired` length — never a measured duration).

The incident is in PR3.6's postmortem under "Process failures this round": the multi-process chaos tests used fixed ports (`const workerPort = 42111`). A run that failed partway left its children alive, so the next run's `host()` saw `exit` before `ready` and rejected with "host exited early" — precisely the symptom of the engine bug that leg exists to catch. Two tests failed, looked exactly like a regression from the commit in hand, and were a leftover process. The fix is `packages/driver/test/chaos-process.test.ts:24`, `const PORT_BASE = 42_000 + (process.pid % 1_000) * 3`, with the reasoning written above it. The same class was already paid for one layer down: `packages/harness/src/ids.ts:9-16` draws ids and tokens from SEPARATE `Rng` streams because a shared stream broke any test predicting a minted id whenever unrelated code took a token — "a false failure that looks exactly like a real one, and it fires precisely when the engine is being refactored, which is when a regression suite most needs to be trustworthy." Why this is correctness and not hygiene: PR3.6's detection ledger records 236 fault-matrix cells, 32 fuzz shards, a 111.8M-state TLC model, the invariant library and eight linters finding **0 of 44** defects while outside review found 37. The machinery's whole remaining value is that its verdicts are believed; once phantom reds are normal, a real violation scrolls by unread.

<!-- review-bot-synopsis:start -->
Flag test-side nondeterminism: a real sleep standing between an action and an assertion about another actor when an observable predicate was available, an engine deadline (lease, backoff, start deadline, wait timeout) crossed by real elapsed time instead of `admin.setFakeNowEpochMs`/the fixture's `advance()`, an assertion whose subject is measured wall time, an assertion that PREDICTS an id/token minted from ambient entropy or from an `Rng` seeded by anything but a literal or loop index, a fuzz/matrix seed-or-step count from `process.env` without the positive-integer `knob()` guard or removal of a progress floor, a numeric literal port bound or handed to a spawned host, a tmp path not built by `mkdtempSync`, and state one `it` writes that a DIFFERENT `it` reads. Pass for deadline-bounded `until()` polls, real-timer yields that reach quiescence before a virtual-clock advance, settle sleeps for OS/socket facts with no observable predicate, wall-clock assertions whose subject is the real-time fallback, a real timer that IS the test's subject (starvation probes, determinism-contract negatives), `systemIdSource()` in the real-process hosts and chaos legs where ids are opaque handles, `new Rng(seed)`/`seededIdSource(new Rng(seed))` in fixture helpers taking seed as a parameter, `Date.now()` used only for timeout bookkeeping, a fixed db basename inside a `mkdtempSync` directory, a port captured from `listen()` and rebound, a module-level cleanup registry read only by `afterAll`, module bindings re-created in `beforeEach`, and floors relocated from per-walk to per-shard aggregate.
<!-- review-bot-synopsis:end -->

Report a failure when the changed code introduces or materially expands any of these:

- **A real sleep standing in for a wait.** `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, N))` (or a `sleep`/`delay` helper) between an action and an assertion about another actor's effect, with no predicate re-checked in between, **when an observable predicate was available**. The repo's wait is a deadline-bounded poll (`until(...)`) that names what it waited for. Decide it by asking whether the very next assertion could have been the poll's predicate; if it could, the sleep is the finding.
- **An engine deadline crossed with real elapsed time.** Expiring a lease, retry backoff, start deadline, `cancellation.maxDurationSeconds` or wait timeout by choosing a small `leaseSeconds`/`inSeconds`/`delaySeconds` and waiting for it, instead of `await f.admin.setFakeNowEpochMs(now + Δ)` or the fixture's `advance()`. Under DESIGN §3.4 rule 3 engine time is database time, so with `fake_now_ms` set, real waiting does not move the engine's clock at all — the test is slow, flaky, and reading a different clock than the code does.
- **Wall time as the subject of an assertion.** `const t0 = Date.now(); …; expect(Date.now() - t0).toBeLessThan(X)`, `expect(elapsed).toBeGreaterThan(X)`, or any threshold whose measured quantity is a duration. The causal observable exists in every layer: `FakeClock.fired`/`sleeps`, `launcher.invocations.length`, `loop.stats`, `SimWorld.trace`, `engineInvariantViolations(f.raw)`, or the rows themselves. (A threshold on a *counter* — ticks, beats, checkpoints — is causal and fine.)
- **An assertion that PREDICTS a value drawn from undeclared entropy.** Flag when a test computes or hard-codes the id, token or key it expects AND that value traces to `Math.random`, `crypto.randomUUID`, `Date.now()`, `process.hrtime`, or `systemIdSource()`. Predicted values must come from `seededIdSource(new Rng(seed))` where the seed traces to a string/number literal or a loop index (`packages/conformance/test/regressions.test.ts:229` mints a deliberate collision this way). Also flag a new draw taken from an `Rng` that another concern already consumes — the separate-streams fix in `packages/harness/src/ids.ts` applies. Using an id only as an opaque handle is not this shape; see Allowed.
- **A seed, step or floor count that can silently reach zero.** A fuzz, fault-matrix or replay-equivalence surface whose seed range or step count reads `process.env` without the positive-integer guard `packages/conformance/test/fuzz-shard-runner.ts:5-13` applies (`knob()`, "refusing a vacuous fuzz run"), or a change removing the progress floor in `packages/conformance/src/fuzz.ts:261-273` or the aggregate per-op floors in `fuzz-shard-runner.ts:58-65`. A green from a surface that ran nothing is indistinguishable from a green from one that proved something.
- **A numeric literal port, or a tmp path not from `mkdtempSync`.** A port written as an integer literal — directly, or via a module constant holding one — then passed to `listen(port)` or to a spawned host, in any test that binds a socket or spawns a process. Ports come from `listen()` with no argument (it binds `:0` and returns the assigned port, `packages/driver/src/http.ts:175`) or from the pid-derived base. Directories come from `mkdtempSync`; a path assembled from `os.tmpdir()`/`/tmp` with a fixed name is the finding.
- **State one `it` writes that a DIFFERENT `it` reads.** A fixture, database handle, server or counter at module scope or in `beforeAll`, where one test's postcondition is another's precondition — or an `it` asserting on rows, ids or ports it did not create. Every store test builds a fresh `:memory:` database per test (`openTestDb()`, `makeLibsqlFixture(seed)`), and vitest parallelizes files onto worker threads, so anything shared across files is a race rather than an order.

Allowed cases (do NOT flag these):

- **Deadline-bounded polls of a real predicate.** `until(...)` in `packages/driver/test/chaos-process.test.ts:43`, `packages/driver/test/e2e.test.ts:82`, `packages/driver/test/loop.test.ts:77` — a bounded loop re-checking an observable that throws a NAMED timeout. The real timer is a retry interval; the assertion is the predicate. The `Date.now()` at `chaos-process.test.ts:44-45` is timeout bookkeeping, not an assertion input. Do not demand a virtual clock: the predicate is produced by a real server or a real child process.
- **Real-timer yields that reach quiescence before the VIRTUAL clock moves.** `packages/sdk/test/run-worker.test.ts:355` spins on `f.clock.fired.length < 2` in 2ms hops so the pass has reached both awaits before `f.advance(30_000)` — advancing earlier would shift the deadlines under test — then asserts `{ kind: 'completed' }` and `beats >= 2`, both causal. `packages/driver/test/loop.test.ts:397` is the same shape inverted: a 25ms sleep bounds `expect(stopped).toBe(false)`, after which the positive is forced deterministically by opening the gate. A bounded negative later forced positive is not a latency assertion.
- **Settle sleeps for an OS or socket fact with no observable predicate.** `chaos-process.test.ts:89,147` let a `SIGKILL`ed child release its socket before a replacement binds; `packages/driver/test/http-hardening.test.ts:57` lets a destroyed socket's teardown be processed before proving the server survived. These wait on facts the process cannot observe. Flag a new sleep here only if an observable predicate was available and skipped.
- **A real timer that IS the test's subject.** `packages/driver/test/loop.test.ts:519-529` schedules a 5ms macrotask to probe event-loop starvation and asserts on `loop.stats.ticks`, a causal counter — the macrotask is the instrument. `packages/harness/test/sim.test.ts:233-243` makes an actor await a 20ms timer to prove the determinism contract DETECTS it (`rejects.toThrow(/determinism contract violation/)`) rather than hanging, then sleeps 30ms so the condemned batch's rejection is handled. A negative-space test of a determinism seam must contain the nondeterminism it refuses.
- **Wall-clock assertions whose subject IS the wall clock.** `packages/store-libsql/test/schema.test.ts:55-70` asserts `nowEpochMs()` is within ±1s of `Date.now()` with no override, and within 5s once `fake_now_ms` is cleared. The point is the real-time fallback, and the tolerances are orders of magnitude above the operation.
- **`systemIdSource()` where ids are opaque handles or the host IS production wiring.** `packages/driver/bin/worker-host.ts:17` and `driver-host.ts:13,18` are composition roots — "the one place the REAL clock and ids are wired" — and the chaos legs at `chaos-process.test.ts:64,125,178` pass `spawned.taskId` back as a lookup key (`WHERE task_id = ?`) without ever predicting its value. Real ids in a real-process leg are the point of the leg.
- **`new Rng(seed)` with a parameter seed in a fixture helper.** `packages/conformance/test/fixture-libsql.ts:9`, `loop.test.ts:64`, `e2e.test.ts:27`, `run-worker.test.ts:50`, `tick.test.ts:14`, `http-hardening.test.ts:14`, `replay-equivalence.test.ts:244` and `packages/harness/src/sim.ts:114` all take `seed` as an argument; the literal lives at the call site (`fx('loop-basic')`, `new Rng(\`fuzz-${seed}\`)`). Follow the seed to its origin before flagging.
- **A fixed database basename inside a `mkdtempSync` directory.** `chaos-process.test.ts:60,121,174` build `join(dir, 'chaos.db')` where `dir` came from `mkdtempSync`. The uniqueness lives in the directory; the basename carries none.
- **A deliberate real sleep inside a spawned host's task body.** `packages/driver/bin/worker-host.ts:28` sleeps `p.stepMs` inside the `chaos-steps` task. The slowness IS the fixture — it gives the chaos leg mid-flight surface to murder. There is nothing to assert here and no clock to advance across a process boundary.
- **A port captured from an ephemeral bind and deliberately rebound.** `packages/driver/test/e2e.test.ts:205` re-listens a replacement worker on `h.workerPort`, a value that came from `listen()` with no argument and is reused because the launcher URL is bound to it. A rebind on a captured port is not a fixed port.
- **A module-level cleanup registry.** `chaos-process.test.ts:12` declares `const children: ChildProcess[] = []`, every `it` pushes to it through `host()`, and only `afterAll` reads it — to kill them. Written by many tests, read by none of them; no test's precondition depends on it.
- **Module-level bindings re-created per test.** `packages/store-libsql/test/schema.test.ts:10-20` declares `let db` / `let admin` at module scope and rebuilds them in `beforeEach` with an `afterEach` close. The binding is shared; the state is not.
- **A floor relocated from per-walk to per-shard aggregate.** `fuzz-shard-runner.ts:53-65` asserts every core transition succeeded somewhere across the shard rather than in every walk, because a per-walk floor pins one unlucky seed as a permanent failure. Aggregating a floor is a determinism FIX — flag removal, never relocation.

When reporting, name three things. First, the seam that already exists and was not used, by file: `admin.setFakeNowEpochMs`/the fixture's `advance()` for engine deadlines, `FakeClock` for SDK and driver sleeps, `new Rng(seed)` + `seededIdSource` for predicted ids, `SimWorld` with a pinned seed for interleavings, `listen()`/`mkdtempSync` for process-scoped resources. Second, the causal observable the assertion should key on instead of the elapsed time or the sleep. Third — the part that matters — say whether the fix uses an existing seam or is evidence of a MISSING one, because CLAUDE.md's red-test rule holds that a bug class which cannot be expressed as a red test is a missing seam to be built first. Never propose "raise the timeout", "add a retry", or "mark it flaky": a retry is the mechanism-shaped form of "inspect more carefully", which the prevention ladder explicitly rules out as a rung. This rule is a detection net of last resort, so a confirmed finding should end by naming the mechanism that would make the shape unwritable — a helper that owns the resource, a fixture that hands out only virtual time, or a lint over these globs.
